distractorExplanations.c: Around 100 to 110 psi is where the governor cuts the compressor back in; cut-out happens higher, at about 125 to 135 psi.
distractorExplanations.a: That is roughly where the low-air warning must activate, far below the governor cut-out point.
distractorExplanations.b: This is below even the cut-in point; the compressor would never stop pumping at a normal level.

distractorExplanations.c: 110 to 115 psi overstates the cut-in point; the CDL manual puts compressor cut-in at about 100 psi, well below cut-out.
distractorExplanations.a: Around 60 psi is the low-air warning point; cut-in happens well above it, near 100 psi.
distractorExplanations.d: That is the governor cut-out range where the compressor stops pumping, not where it resumes.

distractorExplanations.c: 40 to 45 psi is where spring brakes may begin to apply; the low-air warning must come on earlier, before pressure drops below 60 psi.
distractorExplanations.a: About 20 psi is near the bottom of the spring-brake application range; the warning comes much earlier.
distractorExplanations.b: At 30 psi the spring brakes may already be applying; the warning must sound before pressure falls below 60.

distractorExplanations.d: Doubling the allowance for combinations is a common error; with brakes applied the limits are 3 psi/min single and 4 psi/min combination.
distractorExplanations.a: Those are the released-brake leakage limits; with brakes applied the limits are 3 and 4 psi/min.
distractorExplanations.c: Too lenient by 1 psi/min; the applied-brake limit is 3 psi/min single and 4 psi/min combination.

options.a: Within about 10 seconds under test conditions
options.b: Within about 20 seconds under test conditions
options.c: Within about 30 seconds at fast idle under test conditions
options.d: Within about 45 seconds under test conditions

distractorExplanations.c: The test is run at fast idle, but the handbook benchmark for dual systems is 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds, not 30 seconds.
distractorExplanations.a: The handbook standard for dual systems is 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds; 10 seconds is not the benchmark.
distractorExplanations.b: 20 seconds is not the CDL handbook benchmark; dual systems should build 85 to 100 psi within 45 seconds.

options.a: Apply lightly and steadily without lockup
options.b: Pump rapidly on and off before wheels lock
options.c: Apply fully, release as wheels lock, reapply
options.d: Apply fully and hold the pedal down until the vehicle stops

distractorExplanations.d: Holding full pressure locks the wheels and removes steering control; stab braking releases when the wheels lock, then reapplies.
distractorExplanations.a: That is controlled braking; stab braking means full application, release on lockup, reapply.
distractorExplanations.b: Rapid pumping wastes air and is not the stab method; the brakes are applied fully until wheels lock.
